name: Shades Apart
label: Revelation
lede: A summer project from Bridgewater, New Jersey made its first record for $720, turned a Soft Cell staple into an MTV surprise shot in the bassist's backyard, and heard its major-label single on the radio right before Ricky Martin.

eras.title: Seven hundred and twenty dollars at Inner Ear
eras.text: Mark "V" Vecchiarelli, Kevin Lynch and Ed Brown started Shades Apart as a summer project in Bridgewater, New Jersey, raised on The Jam, The Police and The Clash as much as hardcore. Their first record came out on Wishingwell, the label that had put out Youth of Today's Break Down the Walls.

years.h: Shades Apart start as a summer project in Bridgewater, NJ
years.p: Mark "V" Vecchiarelli on guitar and vocals, Kevin Lynch on bass and Ed Brown on drums: the trio that stays together for the band's whole life.

years.h: Shades Apart, made at Inner Ear for $720
years.p: Shades Apart record their debut at [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]'s Inner Ear in Arlington, Virginia, with Zientara and Eli Janney producing, for $720. It comes out on Wishingwell Records in December 1988.
years.xp:
Dave from Vision rode down for gang vocals, and the band treated the whole thing like a road trip. Kevin Lynch remembers grabbing burgers at a place in Arlington that turned out to be the original Five Guys.

They remixed it later at Trax East in South River, New Jersey, in a one-day Fourth of July session with guitarist Mike "Wattage" Demko of TMA helping on guitar tones.

eras.title: College towns and day jobs
eras.text: Shades Apart slowed down while life happened: Ed Brown went off to Virginia Tech, Mark Vecchiarelli became a father. When they came back, they were too melodic for the hardcore kids and too loud for college rock, and they played better in college towns anyway.

q: We always seemed to be somewhere in the middle of all that.
years.h: Neon, five years after Shades Apart's debut
years.p: Neon arrives five years after the first record, made while drummer Ed Brown was at Virginia Tech. Kevin Lynch says Shades Apart always seemed to be somewhere in the middle of hardcore and indie.
years.xp: The Dude Danger EP also came out on Sunspot Records in this period. Mark Vecchiarelli had become a father in 1990.

eras.title: The Descendents' producers and a Soft Cell hit
eras.text: Revelation Records' Jordan Cooper knew Shades Apart from the Wishingwell days and brought them onto the label just as it was widening past youth crew. With Descendents members producing, a cover of Tainted Love got the trio onto MTV.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Save It · REV 40, produced by Bill Stevenson
years.p: Descendents and [[ALL|e92547b5-a134-4149-af9a-c944af9e476f]] members [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] and Stephen Egerton produce Shades Apart at Trax East in South River, New Jersey. Mark Vecchiarelli says their energy in the studio was always on and contagious.
years.xp:
Ed Brown says Jordan Cooper knew the band from the Wishingwell era: Youth of Today had released Break Down the Walls on Wishingwell before Ray Cappo and Cooper started Revelation.

Revelation's first vinyl run was 3,012 black and 309 orange copies, after four black test pressings.

years.h: Shades Apart's Tainted Love becomes a surprise MTV hit
years.p: Shades Apart's cover of Tainted Love, the Gloria Jones song Soft Cell made famous, gets MTV and MuchMusic play. The video was shot in Kevin Lynch's childhood backyard in Bridgewater.
years.xp:
Kevin Lynch says a young Benny Horowitz, later the drummer of [[The Gaslight Anthem|f208f09e-b5b3-4b06-87cd-f7230fae17e3]], is in the video somewhere.

On a MuchMusic appearance, the hosts were expecting Tainted Love and Shades Apart played a different song; the band figures the hosts were pretty mad. AllMusic calls it a surprise 1995 MTV hit.

years.h: Dinner on Sunset next to the guitarist from Bush
years.p: Touring Save It, Ed Brown remembers Shades Apart eating dinner on Sunset Boulevard before a show, seated next to the guitarist from [[Bush|93ccd76c-3790-4435-a8bf-02bc26294b93]].

years.cap: Seeing Things, recorded at the Blasting Room
years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Seeing Things: Shades Apart at the Blasting Room
years.p: Shades Apart make Seeing Things (REV 57) with Jason Livermore at the Blasting Room in Fort Collins, Colorado, while roofers replace the roof and bits of shingle rain down on Ed Brown and Kevin Lynch.
years.xp:
Brown and Lynch were sleeping in the guitar room. Between takes the band jumped off a cliff into Horsetooth Reservoir and got yelled at by a park ranger, someone caught crawdads in the stream by the studio, and Brown held push-up contests with Livermore timed by an old Dr. Beat drum machine.

Lynch says there was no label pressure at all: they felt part of the family.

eras.title: Assholes and restaurants
eras.text: Universal Records signed Shades Apart and got them on rock radio and the American Pie soundtrack. It also sped up their songs without asking, then lost interest, and 9/11 closed the chapter.

years.h: Universal speeds up a Shades Apart song without asking
years.p: For their major-label debut Eyewitness, Universal wanted a radio-proven producer and got Lou Giordano instead of the Descendents crew. During mastering the label sped up one song without permission; the band rejected it.
years.xp: An A&R man told the band himself that A&R was supposed to mean Artists and Repertoire but really meant Assholes and Restaurants. Ron St. Germain mixed part of the record, and Ed Brown remembers watching Shark Week at Giordano's house while everyone else did real work.

years.h: Valentine hits No. 31, right before Ricky Martin
years.p: Shades Apart's Valentine peaks at No. 31 on Billboard's Mainstream Rock chart. On a Florida radio tour, Kevin Lynch hears it on air, followed by Ricky Martin's Livin' la Vida Loca.

years.h: Stranger by the Day lands on the American Pie soundtrack
years.p: Shades Apart's Stranger by the Day is on the American Pie soundtrack. Mark Vecchiarelli remembers watching the movie in a theater, waiting for the credits.

q: 9/11 was kind of like the ending point.
years.p: Shades Apart's second Universal album, with a re-recorded Behind the Wheel from Seeing Things, gets little marketing and less tour support. Mark Vecchiarelli calls it their least favorite recording process.
years.xp: The label also picked a single Kevin Lynch didn't think was the right one. Ed Brown says the band was cooked by then, and Lynch says 9/11 became the point where they turned toward their families' future.

years.h: Shades Apart's Tainted Love turns up in She's Too Young
years.p: The 1995 cover of Tainted Love is used in the 2004 film She's Too Young, while the band is on hiatus.

eras.title: An album written by email
eras.text: Shades Apart never really broke up, they just stopped. A few songs cut back at the Blasting Room in 2011 turned, very slowly, into their first album in nearly twenty years.

years.h: Shades Apart back at the Blasting Room
years.p: Shades Apart return to Jason Livermore's Blasting Room in Fort Collins and record a few songs, the groundwork for their eventual comeback album.
Mark Vecchiarelli, Kevin Lynch and Ed Brown bring Shades Apart back to play shows, the same trio as 1988.
Revelation puts Shades Apart's Save It back on vinyl: 334 opaque orange marble and 766 blue copies.
Mike Demko, the TMA guitarist who helped shape the guitar sounds on Shades Apart's 1988 debut, dies a month before their comeback album comes out.

years.src: No Echo · Punk Rock Theory · Salad Days
years.h: Eternal Echo, Shades Apart's first album in almost 20 years
years.p: Written by email and tracked separately, mixed by Jason Livermore, and released by New Jersey's Hellminded Records. Kevin Lynch places it between Seeing Things and Eyewitness.
years.xp:
The spark was a friend's death: playing his tribute show, Lynch said, reminded them how fragile life is. Ed Brown wrote Souls and Soldiers after the 2017 Women's March in Washington (all three have daughters), and Only Light answers the August 2017 rally in Virginia.

Brown says none of them ever imagined making an album 35 years on.
